questions.question: I saw _____ dog in the park.
questions.explanation: 'A' is used before singular countable nouns when mentioned for the first time.

questions.question: He ate _____ apple for breakfast.
questions.explanation: 'An' is used before words starting with a vowel sound.

questions.question: _____ sun rises in the east.
questions.explanation: 'The' is used for unique things (there's only one sun).

questions.question: I love _____ chocolate.
questions.explanation: No article is used with uncountable nouns when speaking generally.

questions.question: Can you pass me _____ salt, please?
questions.explanation: 'The' is used when both speaker and listener know what is being referred to.

questions.question: She goes to school by _____ bus.
questions.explanation: No article is used with modes of transport after 'by'.

questions.question: He is _____ honest man.
questions.explanation: 'An' is used before 'honest' because the 'h' is silent, creating a vowel sound.

questions.question: We visited _____ United States last year.
questions.explanation: 'The' is used with country names that include 'States', 'Kingdom', or 'Republic'.

questions.question: _____ rich should help _____ poor.
questions.explanation: 'The + adjective' can refer to a group of people as a whole.

questions.question: He was sent to _____ prison for theft.
questions.explanation: No article is used when referring to the purpose of an institution (being a prisoner).

questions.question: She has _____ MBA from Harvard.
questions.explanation: 'An' is used before 'MBA' because 'M' is pronounced with an initial vowel sound.

questions.question: I'll see you _____ next week.
questions.explanation: No preposition or article is used with 'next week', 'last week', etc.

questions.question: This is _____ best movie I've ever seen!
_____ Mr. Smith is waiting outside.
questions.explanation: No article is used before titles with proper names.

questions.question: She arrived _____ hour late.
questions.explanation: 'An' is used before 'hour' because the 'h' is silent.
